system_description.narrative_title: US push to cut Korea drills and revive diplomacy with North Korea
system_description.narrative_summary: A policy shift driven by the U.S. presidency to scale back joint U.S.-South Korea military exercises and pursue renewed diplomacy with North Korea is reshaping regional security calculations. The move has prompted alarm in Seoul, mixed responses from Pyongyang, and intensified diplomatic activity by neighbouring powers, raising questions about deterrence, alliance reliability, and great-power influence in Northeast Asia.
system_description.scope: Decisions and actions affecting the U.S.-South Korea security relationship and deterrence posture on the Korean Peninsula: U.S. presidential directives and Pentagon implementation, joint military drills and readiness, South Korean government and military responses, North Korean political messaging and reactions, regional diplomatic moves (China, Russia), public and elite perceptions of alliance credibility; near-term summit diplomacy as an event driver.
system_description.super_system: Indo-Pacific strategic and security order (great-power competition, alliance networks, nuclear deterrence regimes).
adjacent_subsystems: South Korean domestic politics and defense policy
U.S. domestic politics and presidential foreign policy decision-making
evidence_headlines: Trump instructs Pentagon to reduce military exercises with South Korea
Trump says North Korea's Kim has responded to his overtures
Seoul rattled by threat to drills at heart of US-Korean alliance
China's Foreign Minister Wang Yi to visit South Korea from August 19-20
North Korea Rejects Trump’s Drills-Cut Overture as an Empty Gesture

variables.name: Joint military exercise intensity
variables.description: The scale, frequency, scope, and operational tempo of coordinated military exercises between partner forces.

variables.name: Deterrence credibility
variables.description: The perceived ability and willingness of defensive arrangements to impose unacceptable costs on potential aggressors.

variables.name: Alliance policy alignment
variables.description: The degree of congruence in strategic objectives, threat assessments, and policy choices among allied actors.

variables.name: Military readiness level
variables.description: The aggregate preparedness of deployed and reserve forces to mobilize, deploy, and conduct operations on short notice.

variables.name: Strategic nuclear posture strength
variables.description: The operational deployment, alert levels, and survivability of strategic nuclear forces and supporting command arrangements.

variables.name: Diplomatic engagement rate
variables.description: The frequency, intensity, and diversity of formal and informal diplomatic contacts between rival and regional actors.

variables.name: Crisis miscalculation risk
variables.description: The probability that signaling, movements, or incidents will be misunderstood and lead to unintended escalation.

variables.name: Great-power rivalry intensity
variables.description: The level of strategic competition, influence-seeking, and adversarial interactions among major external powers in the region.

variables.name: Public confidence in security arrangements
variables.description: The population's trust in external commitments and domestic institutions to provide security and uphold agreements.

variables.name: Force integration and interoperability
variables.description: The extent of technical, procedural, and command-and-control integration enabling joint operations across partners.

variables.name: Force posture balance
variables.description: The distribution and mix of military assets across domains, locations, and readiness categories relevant to deterrence and defense.

variables.name: Burden-sharing tension
variables.description: The intensity of disputes and disagreement over allocation of costs, forces, and responsibilities among partners.

variables.name: Regional crisis management capacity
variables.description: The institutional ability and procedural mechanisms available to prevent, mediate, and resolve security crises in the region.

variables.name: Nuclear doctrine clarity
variables.description: The degree to which actors' policies on nuclear use, thresholds, and escalation control are stated, observable, and predictable.

variables.name: Domestic policy pressure
variables.description: The level of internal political demand or pushback for changes to defense posture, alliances, or engagement strategies.

variables.name: Intelligence and surveillance coverage
variables.description: The scope, timeliness, and resolution of intelligence, reconnaissance, and surveillance capabilities relevant to regional activity.

catalysts.title: Halving/shortening of US‑ROK joint drills
catalysts.description: Washington and Seoul implement plans to cut or shorten upcoming combined exercises, reducing scope and duration of scheduled drills.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Seoul, Washington to halve joint drills'; 'US-South Korea military drills to be cut short after Trump order.'

catalysts.title: Attempted Trump–Kim summit this year
catalysts.description: US administration pushes for a high‑level meeting between President Trump and Kim Jong Un, seeking a summit by this fall or year end.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Trump seeks meeting with Kim by this fall'; 'Trump says he plans to meet with North Korea's Kim.'

catalysts.title: China FM Wang Yi visits Seoul (Aug 19–20)
catalysts.description: Chinese foreign minister undertakes talks in Seoul, shaping regional diplomatic dynamics amid US push on North Korea.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'China's Foreign Minister Wang Yi to visit South Korea from August 19-20.'

catalysts.title: North Korean public rejection of US overtures
catalysts.description: Pyongyang publicly dismisses US offers (drill cuts, talks) and frames overtures as insincere, shaping near‑term signaling.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'North Korea dismisses US military drill cuts'; 'North Korea Rejects Trump’s Drills‑Cut Overture as an Empty Gesture.'

catalysts.title: Pentagon planning and implementation of drill cuts
catalysts.description: US military and commanders formalize and execute changes to exercise plans and training schedules following presidential orders.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Trump instructs Pentagon to reduce military exercises'; 'US commander discusses scaling back joint South Korea drills.'

catalysts.title: Seoul's political push for talks / peace process
catalysts.description: South Korean leadership publicly advocates for talks with the North and replacing the armistice with a peace framework, driving diplomatic initiatives.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'South Korea's Lee urges talks with North Korea to replace armistice with peace.'

catalysts.title: Russia–North Korea ties deepen
catalysts.description: High‑level interactions and reaffirmed ties (e.g., Putin–Kim contact) strengthen bilateral links, affecting regional alignment.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'North Korea's Kim, Russia's Putin reaffirm ties on Korean Liberation Day.'
